assumptions.reason: Spec marks these 'to be specified'. Chose values non-binding for AAPL's actual price range but that still cap notional exposure near starting equity.

assumptions.choice: Used the threshold-based signal (0 unless sum>=+2 or sum<=-2) uniformly for both entry gating and the 'close/reverse when final signal changes to opposite' rule, rather than a literal sign(sum).
assumptions.reason: Literal sign(sum) would flip on sum=+/-1, contradicting the spec's own 'otherwise skip/wait' and 'if equal and there is an open position - hold until an exit triggers' clause, which only makes sense if holding survives a non-extreme sum.

assumptions.choice: Implemented reversal as one combined order (size = current position size + freshly computed target size) rather than a separate close then re-entry across two bars.
assumptions.reason: Spec says 'close/reverse' as a single unified action; a single combined order achieves this atomically while still respecting the single-pending-order guard.

assumptions.choice: cooldown_bars gates every order submission (entries, plain exits, and reversals), not just new entries.
assumptions.reason: Spec describes cooldown as an 'order frequency limit... emulates QPS throttle', i.e. an execution-layer constraint on sending any order, not a strategy-side entry filter.

assumptions.choice: min_price/max_price and the notional-cap sizing term are applied only to the side of a trade that opens/increases exposure (fresh entries and the new-position leg of a reversal); a pure close to flatten is never blocked by them.
assumptions.reason: Spec frames these as limits on 'trades'/position value, i.e. entry-side risk controls; blocking an exit on a risk limit would be self-defeating. Still subject to cooldown as noted above.

assumptions.choice: When more than one subsystem's signal agrees with the entry direction, all agreeing subsystems' specific exit conditions are tracked simultaneously; whichever fires first ends the position.
assumptions.reason: Reaching the +-2 aggregator threshold requires at least two subsystems to agree, so 'the subsystem that generated the entry' is often plural; 'the first to trigger in time applies' reads naturally as arbitrating among multiple live exit conditions rather than presupposing a single subsystem.

assumptions.choice: If the aggregate reversal condition and a subsystem-specific exit are both true on the same bar, the aggregate reversal takes priority.
assumptions.reason: Bar-level OHLC data can't establish true intraday ordering; the aggregate signal is the broader/dominant rule so it is used as the tie-break.

assumptions.topic: BB exit as a cross event
assumptions.choice: Implemented the BB middle-band exit with a dedicated CrossOver(close, bb.mid) indicator (fires only on the crossing bar) rather than a simple 'price is above/below mid' level check.
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly says 'cross of the BB middle band', which is a transition event, not a static level condition.

assumptions.choice: entry_price is the actual fill price (order.executed.price) and entry_atr is the ATR14 value read at the bar the order completes; both are fixed at entry and not recomputed afterward for the ATR TP/SL check.
assumptions.reason: Spec defines TP/SL as fixed offsets '... from the entry price', implying a one-time snapshot rather than a rolling recalculation.

assumptions.topic: ATR14 reference bar for breakout signal
assumptions.choice: Used the current bar's ATR14 (self.atr[0]) alongside the previous bar's High/Low for the breakout comparison.
assumptions.reason: Spec names 'prev. High'/'prev. Low' explicitly but is silent on which bar's ATR to use; current-bar ATR is the natural live-indicator reading, consistent with how BB/EMA signals also use current-bar values.

assumptions.choice: The position-size floor of 1 lot is applied unconditionally per the formula, even in the theoretical case where 1 lot's notional would exceed nominal_cap.
assumptions.reason: Spec states the floor as an unconditional minimum ('at least 1 lot'); with nominal_cap=10000 and AAPL's actual price range this edge case does not bind on the given dataset, so no additional clamp was added beyond the literal formula.
